Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production animated sprite sheet for MH Desk Pets
Create EXACTLY TWELVE depictions of ONE Monster Hunter creature, in a perfectly regular FOUR-COLUMN by THREE-ROW grid on a landscape 4:3 transparent canvas. Each equal cell contains one complete SMALL sprite, centered horizontally, sharing a baseline 80% down the cell. Each sprite INCLUDING effects fits inside the central 60% of its cell width and height. Very generous EMPTY alpha gutters between rows and columns and around the outside. Do not enlarge the sprites to fill the canvas. No clipping, no touching neighbors, no grid lines, no text, no labels, no ground, no shadows.
Style: polished highly detailed chibi JRPG monster sprite; crisp dark outline, rich painted pixel-cluster shading, compact cute proportions with a large recognizable head, three-quarter LEFT view. Match a richly shaded 256px desktop companion, not vector, not a simple cartoon. Transparent background with true alpha, not a baked checkerboard.
Maintain exact same character identity, scale, orientation and planted feet across ALL twelve cells. No slide, rotation or camera zoom. All horns, wings, tail and effects must remain well INSIDE each cell.
TOP row = IDLE: relaxed, inhale subtly, brief blink (or head dip for eyeless creature), exhale. 
MIDDLE row = WORKING: four gentle phases of the signature action below, low energy, rising energy, peak, fading. Feet stay planted; no change in limb count or body pose.
BOTTOM row = WAITING: attentive relaxed pose, small upward head tilt, slight curious tilt, settle back. No limb lifting. Every four-frame row loops smoothly back to its first frame.
ANATOMY: preserve the specified limb count exactly. Never draw duplicate old feet/hands beneath moved limbs. Natural occlusion of far-side limbs is good. Wings and forelegs are distinct ONLY when this species has both. Keep all body parts consistent.
